slides.say: For every number x, diamond of x is x to the fifth, plus three x to the fourth, minus two x cubed, plus x squared, plus four x, minus seven. Diamond of two minus diamond of negative two is equal to what?
A long rule, a number and its opposite. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, calculating both, and then a shortcut.

[short pause] Diamond of two. Two to the fifth is thirty-two, three times sixteen is forty-eight, and two times eight is sixteen, with a minus. Thirty-two plus forty-eight is eighty, minus sixteen is sixty-four, plus four is sixty-eight, plus eight is seventy-six, minus seven is sixty-nine.

Diamond of negative two. The odd powers turn negative, and the even powers stay. Negative thirty-two plus forty-eight is sixteen, plus sixteen is thirty-two, plus four is thirty-six, minus eight is twenty-eight, minus seven is twenty-one.
Sixty-nine minus twenty-one is forty-eight. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We look at each term with two and negative two, instead of calculating everything. An even power and the plain number are the same for both, so in the subtraction they cancel. An odd power just changes its sign, and something minus its opposite is twice that thing.

So keep only the odd terms at two, thirty-two minus sixteen plus eight, twenty-four, and double it. Forty-eight. Choice number three. And with a plus instead, only the even terms survive, that's the ninety in the choices. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
